reasoning: Recent Maine Senate polling over the last 45 days shows a very close race, with the most recent reported general-election polls giving Democrat Troy Jackson a small lead over Republican Susan Collins. The best-supported current margin is about D+3, while Cook still rates the seat as a toss-up, which is consistent with a competitive race rather than a stable partisan edge.

sources.name: University of New Hampshire Pine Tree State Poll
sources.details: University of New Hampshire Survey Center poll of likely general-election voters found Troy Jackson leading Susan Collins 49% to 46%, a 3-point Democratic edge.

sources.name: University of New Hampshire Poll via The Hill
sources.details: The Hill’s report on the same UNH poll said Jackson led Collins 49% to 46% among likely general-election voters in Maine.

sources.name: Hart Research / Senate Majority PAC
sources.details: Hart Research, for Senate Majority PAC, found Troy Jackson ahead of Susan Collins 49% to 45% among likely voters, a 4-point Democratic edge.

sources.name: Cook Political Report rating
sources.details: Cook Political Report keeps the Maine Senate race rated as Toss-up, indicating no clear partisan lean from the forecaster’s structural view of the race.
